**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment on Sparkling, which satisfies the preferred position under MINCOMMIT:

- **§11 (Fees)** — payment is limited to the fees set out in the Fee Schedule for the licence and services actually taken; no committed volume or spend.
- **§2 (Grant of License)** — additional fees arise only if we elect to use the Software outside the Authorized Locations, i.e. usage-based, not a commitment.
- **§10 (Maintenance and Support)** — maintenance runs "for a renewable one-year term," so there is no multi-year committed maintenance stream.
- **§17(b)** — we may terminate at any time on ninety (90) days' notice, so even the one-year maintenance period carries an exit.
- Searches for "minimum", "commit", "take or pay", "shortfall", "purchase" and "renew" surfaced nothing resembling a take-or-pay or volume commitment.

Noted for completeness only (not deviations): §3 contains ordinary licence-scope restrictions (no copying beyond backup, no sublicensing, no reverse engineering) — these are scope terms rather than volume caps or purchase commitments, so they fall outside this rule.
